title: Normalized section reduction tensor models
statement:
Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l and a scheme X. Use the canonical scalar presentation and actual section quotient tower of [def-sfb-strict-completion-restriction-data], with a supplied normalized section tensor comparison [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison]. Then the strict reductions admit SectionReductionModels: normalized singleton comparison, derived tensor identification, representative models and the prescribed unit, successor and tensor-model equations. There is no assertion about completion. Precisely:

theorem strictSectionQuotientTensorModels (X : Scheme.{u})
    (T : Presentation.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 1}
      (Modules (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X))
    (data : PrincipalReduction.PrincipalReductionConeData l E X)
    (hdata : data.IsCanonical l E X)
    (hscalar : ∀ (M : Modules (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ)
      (x : M.val.obj U),
      (T.scalar.app M).val.app U x = sectionScalarValue l E X data.d U • x)
    (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (ι : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj (ring (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X) ⟶ B)
    (hB : ∀ n : ℕ, B.obj (op n) = sectionRingSheaf.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        (AdicCompletion.finiteRing l E X n))
    (hι : ∀ n : ℕ, HEq (ι.app (op n))
        (sectionScalarMap.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)))
    (hstep : ∀ n : ℕ, HEq (B.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)
        (sectionScalarMap.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (AdicCompletion.transition l E X n)))
    (H : CoefficientClosedStructure (hom (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X))
    (HM : CoefficientTensorModels.{u, u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      (ring (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X) H)
    (t : TensorComparison (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X H HM) :
      Nonempty (SectionReductionModels l E X T H HM B ι)

proof.text: Use the existing strictSectionQuotientConeMaps to obtain, for each K-flat P, quasi-isomorphisms c_n from the strict cone levels to termwise tensor with B_n. The component formula and T.diagonal imply naturality in P. T.augmentation_level and T.transition, with tensorUnit_levelMap, give the unit and successor squares. Compose Q(c_n) with T.reduction_descent to define the representative model.

Collapse total tensor with N[0] by mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso, followed by the monoidal-to-site tensor identification. Use the existing generator_eq identity from RingedTensorComplexConstraints to identify the prescribed total generator with its pure-tensor summand. On the sole surviving (p,0) summand this is the identity on local pure tensors; sheafification-unit naturality identifies its values with siteSheafTensorTmul. This constructs single and proves single_values without flatness assumptions.

For the supplied HM, take a functorial flat K-flat replacement in both variables. Its natural HM comparison and the invertible localization of the replacement augmentations define a natural map from derived tensor to localized total tensor. K-flat preservation of quasi-isomorphisms makes it invertible when the first variable is K-flat. HM naturality makes it HM.iso.inv when both variables are K-flat. Composing with the singleton comparison gives tensorSingle.

For every K-flat P form model(P) followed by tensorSingle(P).inv. Precompose with the functorial K-flat resolution K and use naturality on chain maps to obtain an isomorphism between K followed by Q and the two derived functors. Conjugate by the invertible localized resolution augmentation to obtain a natural isomorphism on all complexes. Mathlib Localization.liftNatIso descends this isomorphism through Q. Naturality for the augmentation K(P) to P shows its value is the original comparison on every K-flat representative. The unit and successor equations already proved for model supply the corresponding fields. Naturality of the total comparison in q and its equality with HM.iso.inv give tensor_model by cancelling the singleton comparison and inverse model. Assemble the structure.

proof_origin: N2 Lean proof: reuse the separately stated cone maps, construct the ordinary normalized singleton comparison, extend the supplied K-flat tensor comparison by functorial resolution, and descend the natural isomorphism by the fully faithful precomposition with the derived localization. No new sorry statement.
